description: Renovate proposes every dependency update and merges it once every check on the pull request has passed (nothing here requires a check, so Renovate waits for them itself: platformAutomerge is off and it merges on its next run). A new version waits three days after its release (minimumReleaseAge); fixes for vulnerability alerts skip the wait by Renovate's default. timestamp-optional lets an update from a registry that reports no release date through. See https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage

packageRules.description: An image rebuild (a new digest under the same tag) doesn't wait: Docker Hub dates a rebuild by the tag's last push, so a tag rebuilt about weekly would restart the clock each time and never clear the wait.

Node.js stays on the LTS line the project supports (engines >=22.12, the Dockerfile image, CI): a new major is chosen by hand, together with engines and CI, so it is proposed but never merged automatically.

The Node typings follow the oldest Node the project supports (engines >=22.12): with those of a newer major, the typecheck would let through APIs that don't exist there. A new major is chosen by hand, so it is proposed but never merged automatically.
